client.name: Ape Escape 2 Client
client._source: setup guide: "Select the Ape Escape 2 Client from the Archipelago Launcher", and it requires PINE to be switched on in PCSX2. London does carry a PINE bridge (extensions/pcsx2, protocol "pine") -- but a bridge only moves bytes; nothing of ours reads THIS game's memory, so no protocol of ours is established to carry its checks. Recording "pine" here would build a plugin that installs, launches PCSX2 and never reports a check.
client._protocol_source: the world speaks PINE itself: Interface.py connect_to_pcsx2() opens a TCP socket to ("127.0.0.1", 28011) on Windows -- PCSX2's PINE slot -- and a unix socket at pcsx2.sock elsewhere. Recorded as 'unknown' before the PCSX2 bridge existed and never revisited.
client._kind_source: the world ships and registers its OWN client: __init__.py line 20, components.append(Component("Ape Escape 2 Client", func=run_client, component_type=Type.CLIENT)), and Client.py drives the PCSX2 connection directly. London must not read memory for this game.

patch._source: The guide describes no patch file or patching step -- the setup is apworld plus emulator. An absence in the guide is not proof that the world defines no patch, so the model stays unknown.
